items.text: New lab: Gerrymander. Redraw the districts of a state split 25 to 24 and watch the same voters elect a 6 to 1 majority for either side.
New lesson in Comparative Politics: Gerrymandering, from Elbridge Gerry's salamander in 1812 to the 2025 redistricting fights.
Nine more labs get a signature moment with sound: decode with the cipher wheel, call an election night, press a front page, hear a story's arc as a melody, and drill down through deep time.
This screen: a quick look at what's new after each update. Every past update is in Settings under What's New.
Nous now lets you know when a new version is ready, and installs it with one tap.

Every theme redesigned: chalk and a wooden tray on Chalkboard, glowing tubes on Neon, red initials on Parchment, a blinking cursor on Terminal and northern lights on Aurora. Try any of them in the shop before you buy.
The labs have sound, vibration and livelier visuals: drop potassium in water, hear sorting algorithms race, freeze water with one drag.
Lessons and quizzes vibrate to match their sounds. You can turn it off in Settings.
Pages open at the top, buttons are easier to tap, text is easier to read, and spelling is US throughout.

Pick a Card is complete, and free: five new skills after the Key Card. Self-working math tricks, shuffles and controls, the double lift and card forces, misdirection, and the masters from Robert-Houdin to Dai Vernon fooling Houdini.
25 new lessons with step-by-step diagrams, and 82 new sources.
Memory Palace teaches the 2,500-year-old trick behind memory champions, from your first palace to learning a shuffled deck by heart.
Pick a Card starts card magic with the Key Card.
Religion: Prophets, Old and New, and Europe's Old Gods.
All courses now sit together behind one Courses card.
Nearly 600 new sources.
From Scratch, a survival course: fire, water, shelter, first aid, knots, food, navigation, building, chemistry, metalwork and electricity, with 180 diagrams and a real task to try after each lesson.
Lessons and quizzes open full screen, with a clearer answer sheet.
Share cards show your profile icon.
1,400 new sources.
Optional anonymous topic counts, with no ID of any kind. You can turn them off in Settings.
Art lessons have pictures: 87 paintings, sculptures and objects from Lascaux to Malevich, with tap to zoom. Some show what the lesson describes, like Holbein's hidden skull straightened out.
New History topic: the History of Music, from bone flutes to streaming, with raga, gamelan and maqam.
430 new sources across history, biology, math, computing and economics.
New subject: Art. Six topics from cave paintings to a $6.2 million banana, with the secret lives of pigments, forgers and heists, art beyond Europe and an Artists Hall of Fame.
Sociology is now a subject: eight topics on class, crime, gender, race, networks and protest.
Six new History topics: pirates, spies, Vikings, cold cases, shipwrecks and gladiators.
Fixed a quiz counting an answer twice if the app closed mid-question.
Topics you've mastered become collectible cards, framed bronze, silver, gold or prismatic by how far each topic goes. Tap a card to turn it over.
Wear any card you've earned as your avatar, on your profile and the leaderboard.
Hall of Fame figures have their own card art, and you can wear any figure you've unlocked as your avatar.
A redesigned leaderboard: a podium, your standing, and how far everyone has moved since your last visit.
Earned XP flies into your level ring, with a celebration when you level up.
Fixed daily streaks sometimes not counting.
12 new advanced and expert topics, including The Replication Crisis, Ancient DNA, Philosophy of Physics, Deep Earth, Language Phylogenetics and Computational Stylometry.
A new lesson on problem classes, machines and grammars.
1,770 citations from over 1,100 sources, every quote checked against its source. Tap a number in a lesson to see it.
Phase Diagram, Market Sim, Sound Shift, Molecule Builder, Evolution Sim and Particle Sandbox now run on real models.
Every lab and the Hall of Fame checked for accuracy.
Knowledge Graph: tap a topic to see what it needs and leads to, or switch to My topics to see only what you've learned.
80% of topics now cite their sources in the opening lesson.
New subject: Psychology, with eight topics from perception and memory to social and clinical psychology.
40% of topics now cite their sources in the opening lesson.
Fixed 25 facts that sources showed were wrong or out of date.
Missing a topic? Tap Request one to suggest it.
Lessons can show where their facts come from: tap the small number after a claim to see the source, with a link to check it yourself.
Your profile's Topics tab shows only the subjects you've started, each folded away until you tap it.
Fixed two facts that sources contradicted, in Genetics and in Genocide and Atrocity.
The first lesson of every topic now reads like a friend explaining it, and every rewrite was checked against the original for accuracy.
Math displays properly in advanced lessons such as Operator Algebras and the Langlands Program.
Fixed broken symbols in the Cryptography lessons.
Thousands of clumsy sentences fixed across the app, along with mismatched images and broken punctuation.
Spot a mistake? Every lesson section has a Report a mistake link.
A simpler Today panel, and the level bar fills correctly.
A cleaner home screen: your subject's topics come first.
A Today button in the middle of the bottom bar: your streak, today's pick, practice and what to study next, all in one place.
Your level and XP show as a ring in the top corner.
Labs sit below the topics, and the Shop lives in Today.
Latin & Greek Roots, Place Names, Invented Languages and Sanskrit & English.
Monster Panics: vampire exhumations, werewolf trials and the Beast of Gévaudan.
Lost Technologies, How Chips Are Made, The Strange History of Chess, Ant Civilizations and The Mathematics of Folding.
Every lesson fact-checked against sources.
Nous also runs in your browser at nous-9vy.pages.dev, for iPhone and laptop.
A Skip button on setup, for anyone who wants to start exploring straight away.
Share today's fortune cookie as an image.
A fresh welcome screen.
Home appears as soon as the app opens, and math formulas work offline.
Calmer, smoother animations, and locked items dim properly again.
Lessons, quizzes, diagrams and labs match the new look, in light and dark mode.
Fixed the missing Answer in worked examples and the dark box behind lesson images.

title: A fortune cookie for every subject

items.text: The daily fortune cookie now comes from the subject you're studying.
Green is the right answer, and red only marks your own wrong pick.
Fixed score cards vanishing after a quiz, and unreadable Knowledge Graph labels.
A fresh Nous logo and icon, and a warm light theme.
New Religion subject with 14 topics, plus seven new History topics, from life before writing to phantom islands.
A simpler home screen with five tabs.
Backups can be copied and pasted as text.
About 1,200 fact corrections across every subject, checked field by field.
Fixed matching questions where two items share the same answer.
Fixed progress and review mix-ups between similarly named topics.
